calibre: server end to end over HTTP, client clock (eval/client.py steady through baselines/mac/bench.sh), B=1, greedy, ignore_eos, text prompts; 1 warm-up + 3 repeats per server start, 2 starts per system in turns. b1: synthetic 64-token prompts, 1,024 new tokens, token-based decode rate; b1_natural: eval/natural_prompts.py, same rate; b1_chat: GSM8K through the chat template, 256 new tokens, end-to-end rate (see baselines/mac/summarize.py). Microseconds per token.

llamacpp-q4.weights: Q4_K_M GGUF, 18.7 GB: not the checkpoint's formats

llamacpp-q4-ds.draft: mtp.safetensors of the checkpoint (b85c3cf) converted by #32218: convert_hf_to_gguf.py --dspark --outtype bf16

llamacpp-q4-pr.note: check that #32218 leaves plain decode as master (it does: 40.0 tok/s)

mlxlm-native.weights: the checkpoint's own formats: the like-for-like (track A/C) reference
mlxlm-native.note: no ignore_eos in mlx_lm.server: synth/natural streams may stop early (--allow-short, all streams ran >=64 tokens); one server start for synth and natural (the first start failed on the model name)

omlx-oq4e.weights: oQ4e: NVFP4 experts of layers 0-19 as stored, layers 20-23 experts MXFP8 -> affine 4-bit, attention/embeddings affine 8-bit

omlx-oq4e-ds.flags: as omlx-oq4e with mtp_enabled true (bundled BF16 DSpark draft, block 8, adaptive depth up to 7)
omlx-oq4e-ds.note: streams one SSE chunk per ~128 ms (9-15 tokens) without per-chunk counts: the token-based rate spreads each stream's tokens evenly over its chunks

notes: No general engine here runs the checkpoint's formats with speculation: mlx-lm #2086 has no DSpark; oMLX and llama.cpp speculate on re-quantized weights (oQ4e, Q4_K_M). A track-C engine on the checkpoint's own formats is compared with mlxlm-native (same formats) and with the fastest practical engine (omlx-oq4e-ds).
